links.outcome: Slot F1 excluding initial greeting and refusal rate under indirect contamination, with vs without sanitizing defense
links.effect: Indirect contamination cut slot F1 excl. init to 0.489 (95% CI 0.398-0.581) with refusal rate 0.047. With defense it returned to 0.903 (95% CI 0.880-0.926), refusal rate 0.000.
links.quote: In this benchmark, indirect contamination of external context was the dominant failure mode, whereas a simple sanitizing defense restored performance.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating educational availability (continued usable training dialogue) as a first-class outcome alongside safety for LLM virtual patients
Threshold-based guard design evaluated by post-hoc replay on logged dialogues

screen.practice: prompt sanitizing defense and threshold-based guards against instruction contamination
screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks the robustness of an LLM-based virtual patient under adversarial/instructional contamination and tests whether safety defenses/sanitization restore educational availability and safety.
